title: Using rhythmCI: A Quick Guide
text: Understanding rhythmic patterns essential uncovering time-dependent biological processes. However, analyzing rhythmicity gene expression datasets can complex, involving normalization, statistical modeling, careful visualization. rhythmCI package designed simplify steps. provides streamlined workflow : Load normalize Nanostring nCounter data Perform rhythm analysis using Harmonic Regression method Estimate confidence intervals amplitude Generate informative visualizations vignette introduces core functions rhythmCI demonstrates use typical time-series Nanostring nCounter dataset. end guide, able perform complete rhythm analysis raw data visualization. designed gene expression data, functions rhythm analysis, confidence interval estimation, visualization broadly applicable can used types biological data, including proteomics.

title: Rhythmicity analysis using Harmonic Regression and bootstrapping — rhythmicity
text: list subject containing following: lower (ci.lower) upper (ci.upper) value confidence interval amplitude, rhythmic status variable (rhythmicity), mesor harmonic regression (hr.mesor), amplitude harmonic regression (hr.amplitude), phase harmonic regression (hr.phase).

title: Rhythmicity analysis using Harmonic Regression and bootstrapping — rhythmicity
text: matrix samples across time rows columns variables provided perform harmonic regression. regressing data cosine functions, best fit residuals obtained. residuals sampled replacement using bootstrapping. instance bootstrapping, sampled residuals summed best fit yielding bootstrap estimate amplitude. Confidence Interval (CI) amplitude estimates computed using provided alpha value (also includes Bonferroni correction). Using CI fc_cutoff rhythmic status variables defined follows: rhythmic (lower upper CI lies cutoff), arrhythmic (lower upper CI lies equal cutoff) inconclusive (lower upper CI straddles cutoff). obtained mesor (average value), amplitude, phase estimated bootstrapping. Please note least 4 samples needed per subject. variables least 4 samples analyzed. column-wise operation need time matrix-wise operation.
